title: Helena in Jerusalem
hookLine: the emperor's mother builds churches at the holy places; tradition says she found the cross

cards: The emperor's mother is packing for a long road east. Her name is Helena, and her son is Constantine. She could send architects.
She could send gold and a letter with the imperial seal. Instead she goes herself, to the land where the Gospels happened.
Bishop Eusebius, who wrote a life of her son, says she went to give thanks and to pray in the places where the Savior had walked. Not a tour of inspection. A pilgrimage.

teach.b: Start with what Eusebius tells us. Helena dedicated two churches: one over the cave at Bethlehem where, Christians said, Jesus was born, and one on the Mount of Olives, at the place of the ascension.
The aim was to mark the spots where God had come close, so pilgrims could stand there too.

Second, the road. Eusebius says she gave freely as she traveled: to whole towns, to soldiers, to people with nothing to wear, to prisoners, some of whom she set free. In church she didn't sit apart in imperial splendor.
She came in plain clothes and prayed among ordinary worshippers. Third, the story that travels with her name.

Tradition says that in Jerusalem Helena searched for the cross of Christ, and found it. Here it helps to be honest about the sources. Eusebius, who describes her journey and her churches, says nothing about a cross.
The story of the finding appears in later writers, among them Saint Ambrose of Milan. The Church honors relics of the cross, and the feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross recalls them.
Catholics and Orthodox Christians honor Helena as a saint, whatever a historian decides about the details. Fourth, why her trip still matters.

teach.h: LET US GO OVER TO BETHLEHEM.
teach.b: In Luke's Gospel, after the angels leave, the shepherds say: "Let us go over to Bethlehem, and let us see this word that is come to pass." Eusebius says Helena made her journey in old age.
Like the shepherds, she didn't settle for hearing about it.
She went to see. And Christians still live in Bethlehem, Jerusalem and Nazareth, and still pray in churches near the places she marked.

how: Catholics honor Saint Helena as a saint, and pilgrims still travel to the churches at the holy places in Bethlehem and Jerusalem; parishes often take up collections for Christians in the Holy Land.

games.why: Eusebius says she made the journey herself, prayed at the holy places, and dedicated churches at Bethlehem and on the Mount of Olives.

practice: Picture Bethlehem, Jerusalem and Nazareth, towns where Christian families worship near the old holy places, alongside neighbors of other faiths: one street, one church door, one family getting ready for Sunday.
If you pray, pray for Christians in the Holy Land and for peace for everyone who lives there; if you don't, simply keep them in mind, one town at a time.

wordCard.voice: Helena in Jerusalem. The emperor's mother who traveled to the holy places, built churches, gave to the poor, and, tradition says, found the cross. Today's word.
